# dsh-intelligent-ui
Interactive cards in DeepSeek Harness chats. The model writes a small interface program, the chat dr
aws it as a native card, and every control recomputes in your browser without another model call. A
button sends its text as your next message.
中文

| Requires | DeepSeek Harness **>= 0.2.1-rc.1** (below 0.3.0) |
| Platforms | Web UI, macOS desktop

app, and Windows desktop app — one bundle, because both desktop apps load the same web client |
| Ve

rified | Web UI 0.2.1-alpha.4; macOS and Windows desktop apps 0.2.1-rc.2 |
| Install | Settings → Pl
ugins → Add plugin → `https://github.com/StarsHarryZhu/dsh-intelligent-UI` (needs `git` on `PATH`),
then restart the harness and reload the page |
## How it works
- The plugin registers one tool, `ui_render`, and one skill, `dsh-intelligent-ui`, which teaches the
model when a card beats prose. The skill is its own part of the plugin: the Plugin Manager lists it
with its own switch, and installing the plugin installs it. The model never writes HTML or JavaScri
pt: its program is checked against the 35-component catalog and stored with the tool result. SVG it

writes for a drawing is read into a checked tree with no scripts, styles, links, or images.
- A card
draws in the tool row while the reply streams, and under the reply once it finishes. Moving a contr
ol recomputes every figure locally, and this browser keeps what you set, so a reload shows the card

as you left it.
- Asked to change a card, the model draws a revised one that starts from your settin

gs; the earlier card says a newer version follows.
- A `player` animates a card: code traced line by
line, an algorithm's passes, a point moving along a curve. With `loop=true autoplay=true` a drawing
plays by itself while it is on screen, like a GIF: a rolling wheel, a travelling wave, an orbit. Pl
ayback runs in the browser and sends nothing to the model, and nothing starts by itself if your syst

em asks for less motion.
- A `canvas` draws what the model sketches, from shape lines or SVG. You ca
n drag its points and click its parts, and everything recomputes locally; a button can tell the mode

l what you chose.
- Cards compute integrals (including infinite bounds), derivatives, limits, sums a
nd products, roots, and Taylor polynomials. A value that cannot be computed reliably shows "—", neve

r a guess.
- Uninstalling leaves every session opening as before; earlier calls show as ordinary too

ss.
- Uninstalling leaves every session opening as before; earlier calls show as ordinary tool rows.

`AGENTS.md` holds the rules of the tree; `docs/VERIFY.md` is the live checklist.
## The 35 components
One card per component, drawn by this plugin in the host's light theme. The program behind each card
is in `docs/SAMPLES.md`.
### `card` — Layout
The framed root: optional title, padding, and gap.
### `col` — Layout
A vertical stack in reading order.
### `row` — Layout
Equal-width cells side by side; they wrap on a narrow screen.
### `grid` — Layout
An even grid of one to four columns.
### `tabs` — Layout
Pages the reader switches between, by click or arrow key; only the open page is drawn.
### `tab` — Layout
One page of `tabs`, labelled by its title; pages share the card's state.
### `title` — Text
A headline line in five sizes.
### `text` — Text
A sentence, with `{…}` live values.
### `badge` — Text
A one-word status label in five tones.
### `callout` — Text
One emphasized remark: an assumption, a caveat, a next step.
### `divider` — Text
A hairline separator.
### `link` — Text
A citation link, opened only when clicked.
### `image` — Text
An inline `data:` image with alt text and a caption.
### `code` — Text
Code or other preformatted text, kept exactly as written, with syntax colours in the host's palette,
line numbers, a copy button, and `current=` highlighting the running line.
### `metric` — Data
One prominent number that recomputes as controls move.
### `progress` — Data
A proportion bar.
### `table` — Data
A comparison table; `current=` highlights a row, and `sortable=true` lets the reader sort by any col
umn. Any table copies as CSV or Markdown; past 8 rows it gains a filter, and past 20 it pages.
### `keys` — Data
Label and value pairs for exact figures.
### `list` — Data
A bulleted list; `current=` highlights an item.
### `steps` — Data
A numbered procedure; with `mono=true` and `current=`, a code listing with the running line highligh
mbered procedure; with `mono=true` and `current=`, a code listing with the running line highlighted.
### `chart` — Data
A bar, line, area, or pie chart of one `values=` series, or of up to four `series` lines.
### `series` — Data
One named series of a chart, stacked or side by side; the legend hides and shows it, and a readout n
ames one column's figures.
### `diagram` — Data
A flowchart laid out in layers; loops return along the side, and `current=` highlights a box.
### `canvas` — Data
A drawing: `shape` lines over an optional SVG, which is read into a checked tree. Pictured with one
hape` lines over an optional SVG, which is read into a checked tree. Pictured with one area clicked.
### `shape` — Data
One thing on a canvas: a line, rectangle, circle, polygon, path, curve of a function, text, point, i
nvisible area to click, or a part of the SVG placed by its id. Coordinates, turns, sizes, and fades
are expressions, so a player animates them; a `point` with `drag=true` moves under the reader's poin
ter, and a click stores a value in a state.
### `plot` — Math
Curves of y = f(x) with a marked point, its tangent, and a shaded integral.
